rationale: The student added tens (3+2=5) and ones (7+6=13) independently and wrote them side by side as 513 instead of regrouping 10 ones into 1 ten. The 'make-a-ten' place-value piece demonstrates bundling 10 ones into a single ten.
intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [14]. Tutor points at: 10 ones bundling into 1 ten

frames.caption: Here are 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 4 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 4 in the ones place: 14. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not understand that only one digit fits in the ones place and 10 ones bundle into 1 ten. This short demo specifically addresses bundling 14 ones into 1 ten and 4 ones, isolating the concept using a clean visual demonstration without the complexity of a full two-digit addition problem.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this is an ideal short demo to show why you cannot write two digits in the ones place and how regrouping works.
